title: Loop Seeded Defect Registry
description: Registry of intentionally seeded defects used to validate the detection capability of Loop's AI roles (quality-engineer, security-engineer, test-engineer, architect, independent-reviewer). Each entry maps a known defect to its expected detector and defines the false-negative impact if the defect is missed.

defects.title: SQL Injection via f-string query building
defects.description: The search_users method constructs a SQL query using an f-string with user-supplied keyword directly interpolated. No parameterization is used, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL via the keyword parameter.
detection_mechanisms: manual code review: string-formatting + sql pattern
defects.false_negative_if_missed: P0 — Attacker can exfiltrate or destroy all user data through SQL injection.

defects.title: Missing input validation on user creation
defects.line_hint: create_user method — no validation on username/password/email
defects.description: The create_user method accepts username, password, and email without any validation: no emptiness check, no email format validation, no password length/complexity requirements, no sanitization against injection attacks.
detection_mechanisms: manual code review: missing guards before db write
test coverage: boundary tests for empty/null/malformed inputs
defects.false_negative_if_missed: P1 — Invalid or malicious data enters the database, causing downstream corruption and potential XSS when rendered.

defects.title: Plaintext password storage
defects.line_hint: set_password method — password stored without hashing
defects.description: The set_password method writes the raw password string to the database without any hashing (bcrypt, argon2, scrypt, or even SHA-256). A database breach exposes all user passwords in plaintext, enabling credential-stuffing attacks across other services.
defects.false_negative_if_missed: P0 — Database compromise reveals all user plaintext passwords, enabling widespread account takeover.

defects.title: Division by zero on empty input list
defects.description: The get_average_age method divides by len(user_ids) without checking whether the list is empty. An empty input list raises ZeroDivisionError, causing an unhandled 500 error in any API endpoint that calls this function.
detection_mechanisms: unit test: boundary case with empty list input
defects.false_negative_if_missed: P2 — Unhandled exception causes API 500 errors when querying empty user sets.

defects.title: N+1 query in loop
defects.description: The get_users_with_orders method fetches orders for each user inside a loop, resulting in N+1 database round-trips. For 1000 users, this makes 1001 queries instead of 1 with a JOIN. Under load, this causes severe latency and database connection exhaustion.
detection_mechanisms: manual code review: query inside iteration
defects.false_negative_if_missed: P1 — Performance degrades quadratically with user growth, causing timeouts under normal load.

defects.title: Circular module dependency between services
defects.line_hint: OrderService references UserService, UserService references OrderService
defects.description: UserService and OrderService mutually reference each other at the type level (OrderService.__init__ accepts UserService, UserService.set_order_service accepts OrderService). This creates a circular import dependency that prevents independent testing, deployment, and can cause import-time errors.
detection_mechanisms: manual architecture review: dependency graph analysis
defects.false_negative_if_missed: P2 — Modules become tightly coupled, preventing independent deployment and increasing regression risk.

security-engineer.description: Responsible for detecting security vulnerabilities including injection attacks, unsafe credential handling, and insecure data storage.

quality-engineer.description: Responsible for detecting quality issues including missing validation, error handling gaps, and code hygiene problems.

test-engineer.description: Responsible for detecting logic errors, boundary condition failures, and untested code paths through test design.

architect.description: Responsible for detecting architecture violations including performance anti-patterns, coupling issues, and structural violations.

independent-reviewer.description: General-purpose reviewer that should catch a broad range of issues across all categories.

beginner.description: Any competent developer should detect these within a standard code review.

intermediate.description: Requires careful review and understanding of context; may need tooling assistance.

advanced.description: Requires domain-specific expertise (DB performance, architecture patterns) to identify.
